hypothesis: Two fresh independent participants can create more verifier-accepted candidate diversity than one capable participant using sequential self-reflection under the same two-model-call budget.
strongBaseline: single-reflect: one participant, first candidate, visible-only feedback, second revision candidate, then the same independent verifier and deterministic Join over both candidates.
candidate: multi-independent: two participant identities, each receives the same frozen visible Task independently, one model call each, then the same independent verifier and deterministic Join over both candidates.

multiPromotionRule.development: multi accepted Goals must exceed baseline accepted Goals
multiPromotionRule.holdout: multi accepted Goals must exceed baseline accepted Goals
requiredSafety: all accepted joins survive partial-result Host reopen
multiPromotionRule.meaning: A tie, mixed split, smaller gain, excessive cost, or coordination regression is insufficient to justify a new Multi-Agent capability layer.

claimLimit: At most one bounded repository-repair evidence family; positive evidence would justify retaining a participant-branch pattern, not a generic Agent society or scheduler.
